text:
Sam: Quick thread — thinking about API key + RBAC model for public API, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Two high-level options: (A) org-scoped master keys + project-level bindings, (B) project-scoped keys only. Main concerns: key rotation, least-privilege for 3rd-party integrators, auditability, and service-to-service auth for internal jobs. :thinking:

Marta: I lean toward org-scoped keys for humans (convenience) + project-scoped service tokens for infra. org keys create fewer objects but we must enforce project bindings server-side (policy layer). avoids a zillion keys per project.

Priya: For Private deployments we can't assume central KMS availability. Recommend short-lived JWTs signed by customer-managed KMS/HSM, with token-exchange endpoint to mint project-scoped tokens. Sketch of token format: `{"iss":"redwood-svc","sub":"svc-account:ingest","aud":"project:acme-123","exp":<unix>}`. Rotate signing keys via KMS and publish JWKS.

Dan: +1 on short-lived JWTs. For public API keys we should still support long-lived API keys but require them to be bound to an owner and a scope list (projects + allowed-ops). Add metadata fields: owner, purpose, rotation_policy. That enables automated pruning. :+1:

Sam: How do we map RBAC roles? baseline suggestion: org-admin, org-reader, project-admin, project-deployer, project-reader, service-invoke. Should API keys inherit roles or be separate role grants?

Marta: Prefer explicit grants per key (list of role bindings) rather than implicit inheritance. Simpler to reason about and avoids surprise privilege escalation when org roles change. Also implement role precedence rules and deny-listing.

Priya: Also consider service accounts vs user API keys: service accounts get machine-only flags, shorter default TTL, and mandatory rotation. Example policy snippet for binding a key to a project: ```policy: {"subject":"key:xxxx","bindings":[{"role":"project-deployer","resource":"project:acme-123"}]}```

Dan: We should support attribute-based checks later (ABAC) for things like environment=prod tag. For now RBAC + resource scoping is fine. Also enforce that keys with deploy privileges cannot be used from unknown IPs by default (policy option).

deploy-bot: RFC created: /rfc/authn-authz-token-lifecycle (draft) — please review and comment.

Sam: One more angle — cross-org partner integrations. We need a token-exchange flow (OAuth2-like) to mint short-lived tokens with constrained scopes and audit trails. Explicit trust setup per partner.

Marta: Agree. Also surface token usage in Console with last-used, callers, and ip. That will help security reviews.

Priya: I'll draft the token lifecycle section (issuance, rotation, revocation, offline revocation for Private). Dan — can you capture the RBAC role table? Sam — can you draft the key metadata schema? I'll add JWKS/KMS notes.

Sam: Sounds good. I'll start a follow-up RFC skeleton and paste links here when ready. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
